$comment: Machine-readable data-ownership matrix — source of truth for the C1 write guard (guard.ts/client.ts, BE-mono-13) and the check-ownership CI rules (bin/check-ownership.mjs, OPS-mono-14). Generated by hand from project-docs/03-architecture-design.md §1 (the live matrix, already corrected for the 3 reader fixes and worker-undangan's `clients` removal) plus project-docs/12-cross-repo-integration-design.md §6.2 (planned 0013-0021 deltas on top of the live 0001-0012 migration lineage in migrations.lock.json). Do not hand-edit without updating both docs' pointer notes. `writers` is a map of appName -> writable columns for that table ("*" = no column restriction, any column). `readers` is a ceiling, not an obligation (doc 03 §1). Tables/columns marked planned-only in a `note` are not yet in the live 0001-0012 schema; they are included now so the matrix and its generated guard rules don't need a breaking change when 0013+ lands.

orders.note: Live since 0009_orders_activation.sql. Checkout -> Midtrans -> webhook -> provisioning, owned end-to-end by worker-landing. Planned additive column under 0015_orders_status_log.sql: client_idempotency_key (UNIQUE) — still covered by worker-landing's unrestricted '*' write.

order_status_log.note: PLANNED — not in the live 0001-0012 lineage. Lands as 0015_orders_status_log.sql per doc 12 §6.2. Append-only payment audit trail, owned by worker-landing alongside orders.

order_refunds.note: BE-mono-26 (approved by Pram). PLANNED — the table does not exist yet: it is proposed in doc 17 section 13.6/FR-14 and will be created by BE-wl-34's migration (not yet in migrations.lock.json); declared here ahead of the migration because no check-ownership rule (R1-R7) cross-checks ownership.json against migrations, only consumers' schema mirrors against the matrix (R5). worker-admin creates and progresses every refund (INSERT + UPDATE, unrestricted '*'; no bank details are stored) from the staff queue (BE-admin-19). worker-landing is READ-only, solely to reconcile Midtrans refund notifications against a refund record (BE-wl-38); it writes nothing here (if BE-wl-38 must write a gateway status into this table that needs a separate grant, NOT given here: it records on orders.gateway_status instead). worker-user and worker-undangan have NO access. ownership.json has no verb scoping, so read-only for landing is expressed by omission from writers.

clients.note: BE-mono-22 (approved by Pram): worker-admin also creates clients rows in its real provisioning flow (POST /api/clients: id/name/email/phone/password_hash/created_at) on behalf of a client who has not self-served; it still must NOT write token_version or the activation_* columns. Shared-write table (doc 03 §1). worker-landing creates the row at provisioning and re-issues the activation token; worker-user owns password/token_version/profile after activation — it must never write activation_token_hash/activation_expires_at/activation_issued_at/activation_resend_count. `activation_issued_at`/`activation_resend_count` are AUTHORED in 0019_activation_observability.sql and `updated_at`/`deleted_at` in 0015_soft_delete_audit_columns.sql (locked in migrations.lock.json, not yet applied to the remote D1 — see landing project-docs/16-migration-rollout-plan.md). RESOLVED (2026-09-17, was a JUDGMENT CALL): `deleted_at` is owned by worker-admin, not worker-user — account deletion is ops-initiated (support/GDPR-style request), not self-service. Rationale: no self-service account-deletion endpoint exists or is designed anywhere in worker-user's endpoint contract (doc 03 §'worker-user — endpoint contract' has no DELETE /api/account or equivalent); the sibling `invitations` table already sets this exact precedent in this same matrix — `invitations.deleted_at` is worker-admin-owned ops-override, not worker-user, despite worker-user being invitations' primary content-editing writer, so client-level soft-delete should follow the same ops-driven pattern for consistency. worker-admin moves from reader to writer (column-scoped to `deleted_at`/`updated_at`, not `*`) — per this file's own convention (see `invitations`/`guests`), an app scoped to specific writable columns is listed only under `writers`, not duplicated in `readers`, since write access implies the read access needed to perform the write; worker-admin's existing `GET /api/clients`, `/api/clients/:id` lookup (doc 03 §7) is unaffected by removing it from the `readers` ceiling list. worker-undangan is intentionally NOT a reader here — doc 12 §5.3 resolves its `clients` disposition by removing the dead table object from its schema mirror (folded into BE-undangan-07) rather than granting a read. BE-mono-33 (2026-09-24, approved by Pram): worker-user gains activation_token_hash and activation_expires_at. It CLEARS both to NULL on activation (auth.service.ts's `activate`), which IS the replay defence security/activation-replay.test.ts covers — without the grant, activation cannot consume its own token. Found the same way as the invitations gap, by forcing `throw`. THE LIMIT OF THIS GRANT, stated because it matters: ownership.json is column-scoped, not value-scoped, so it cannot say "may set to NULL only". A write of a REAL hash from this Worker would be an account-takeover primitive — which is exactly why worker-landing's own repository calls the column creator-only. The value scope is enforced in CODE instead, by invitation-worker-user/scripts/check-activation-writes.mjs, which fails CI on any assignment other than null; same pattern as landing's check-password-hash-writes.mjs.

invitations.note: `checkin_test_mode` (INTEGER 0/1, AUTHORED in 0023_checkin_test_mode.sql, doc 17 FR-22/ruling 40) is the owner-only check-in test-mode toggle: worker-user writes it via the owner-facing toggle endpoint (FR-22.1). worker-admin also gets this one column so its EXISTING add-on-revoke path (FR-8.2, PATCH /invitations/:id/addons, which already writes purchased_addons) can flip it back to 0 in the same action when staff revoke the qrcheckin add-on (ruling 40 point (e) / OQ-35 = revoke turns test mode off) — a minimal widening of a table worker-admin already writes, not a new table grant. NOT extended to worker-admin: any write/read access to `guests` — erasing the outstanding TEST check-ins that must accompany turning test mode off (OQ-34 = full erase, doc 17 FR-22.4; see the `guests` table note) still requires a worker-user-owned write path (e.g. a sweep the next time worker-user touches that invitation's guests), because worker-admin has no presence at all in `guests` ownership today and gaining one is a materially bigger widening than one column on a table it already writes. Flagged for architecture-analyst/Pram, not decided here: if the admin revoke must erase those rows synchronously in the same request (rather than via a worker-user-owned sweep), that needs a SEPARATE, explicit ownership widening granting worker-admin column-scoped write on `guests.checked_in_at`/`checked_in_is_test`. BE-mono-24 (OQ-1 = B, approved by Pram): `purchased_addons` (nullable JSON, e.g. {"gallery":2,"qrcheckin":1}, parsed by tier.ts `parsePurchasedAddons`) is written by worker-landing (at provisioning/creation only — enforced by landing's provisioning service and repository types, not by this column list, which cannot express row-scoped rules) and worker-admin (column-scoped ops edit, PATCH /invitations/:id/addons). worker-user and worker-undangan only READ it: worker-user is deliberately NOT given the column in its writer list, so the runtime guard rejects any user-side write; worker-undangan is a reader; a writer implies read access per this file's convention. The column itself is AUTHORED by BE-wl-27 (next free migration, not yet in migrations.lock.json). BE-mono-22 (approved by Pram): worker-admin also creates invitations (POST /api/invitations: id/client_id/template_id/slug/event_type/title/status/created_at/updated_at) and toggles addons via settings (PATCH /invitations/:id/addons); it still must NOT write content columns (opening/story/quote/music_*/wa_template) or activated_at/expires_at. Shared-write table (doc 03 §1): worker-landing creates at provisioning, worker-user edits/publishes, worker-admin does ops-override only. worker-landing reads for demo-slug resolution in catalog.ts's loadStore() (one of the 3 reader corrections). `package_tier`/`activated_at`/`expires_at` are AUTHORED in 0014_invitation_tier_duration.sql (renumbered from doc 12's 0013, which was taken by orders idempotency); `photo_cap_override` in 0018_photo_cap_override.sql; `deleted_at` in 0015_soft_delete_audit_columns.sql (all locked, not yet applied to the remote D1). `event_type` is listed under its live name and stays writable: BE-wl-04 (2026-09-21) authored the event_type->event_label migration as `0026_event_label_rename.sql` (0019 was already taken by 0019_activation_observability.sql by the time this landed — see landing project-docs/16-migration-rollout-plan.md §12 for the renumbering note), purely additive (`invitations.event_label` TEXT nullable, backfilled from `event_type` as plain text; the old column is NOT dropped — that is BE-wl-06, gated on a production burn-in after BE-wl-05 and worker-admin's own provisioning-path deploy per doc 12 §6.2's add->backfill->deploy->drop sequencing). `event_label` is added here to the SAME three writers as `event_type` (worker-landing, worker-user, worker-admin) ahead of any of them actually writing it — matching this file's own precedent of granting a write capability at migration-authoring time (e.g. `checkin_test_mode` in 0023/v0.9.0) rather than gating the grant itself on remote apply or code deploy; only the Drizzle `schema.ts` mirror in each app repo is deferred until the code that first uses the column ships (per doc 16 §3 step 5), since an early schema-mirror column (not an early ownership grant) is what would break a production `select()`. No app has shipped code writing `event_label` yet (BE-wl-05 for worker-landing; worker-admin's own equivalent change is unscheduled here — see BE-wl-06's note on the second call site) — until then this grant is inert, exactly like `checkin_test_mode` was between its own authoring and BE-user/BE-admin shipping their toggle endpoints. JUDGMENT CALL: 'worker-landing must never write package_tier on an invitation it didn't just create' (doc 03 §1) is a temporal/row-scoped rule a static per-app column allowlist can't express — package_tier is listed as writable by worker-landing here because it must be set at creation; the creation-only constraint is a business-logic concern for BE-mono-13's guard or worker-landing's own service layer, not something ownership.json's column list can encode. `is_demo` (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, 0/1) is AUTHORED in 0022_invitation_is_demo.sql (locked in migrations.lock.json) and is deliberately in NO app's writer allowlist: the guard therefore rejects every app's write to it, and it is set only by ops SQL (OPS-wl-08). All four apps (worker-user, worker-undangan, worker-admin, worker-landing) may READ it - table-level reader/writer access already covers that, so no readers change was needed. JUDGMENT CALL: worker-admin's exact 'ops override only' column set is not enumerated in doc 12/03 prose beyond the phrase itself — scoped conservatively to lifecycle/tier/soft-delete fields; flag for system-analyst if broader ops fields are needed. BE-mono-33 (2026-09-24, approved by Pram): worker-user gains the five CREATION columns id/client_id/template_id/slug/created_at. It has always created invitations (modules/invitations/invitations.repository.ts's `create`), and this matrix granted it every content column but not the primary key — a creator that may not write `id` cannot create. The gap was invisible because worker-user runs the guard in `warn` mode, which LOGS the violation and runs the statement anyway; it surfaced only when QA-shared-16 forced `throw` and 30 tests failed across 13 files. The code was right and the matrix was incomplete.

sections.note: BE-mono-22: worker-admin also INSERTs the 12 default sections when it provisions an invitation on a client's behalf (POST /api/invitations, buildDefaultSections). Original note: Two writers but no column split needed, unlike clients/invitations/guests (doc 03 §1 only calls out those three as needing column-scoped writes): worker-landing seeds the 12 default sections at provisioning (INSERT), worker-user edits afterward (UPDATE) — sequential, not concurrent, and no security-sensitive columns exist on this table.

persons.note: Honoree records, edited only via worker-user's content CRUD.

events.note: Ceremony/reception records, edited only via worker-user's content CRUD. worker-admin reads this table (read-only) for the eventAt countdown on invitation views.

photos.note: worker-admin's read access is scoped in practice to `r2_key` only, for the media-retention cron (BE-admin-13) — one of the 3 reader corrections. The matrix's reader ceiling is table-level, not column-level (doc 03 §1: 'readers are a ceiling, not an obligation'), so worker-admin is technically free to read other columns of this table; it is documented here as not needing to.

story_items.note: "Our Story" timeline items, edited only via worker-user's content CRUD.

gift_accounts.note: Destination bank/e-wallet accounts, edited only via worker-user's content CRUD.

guests.note: `checked_in_is_test` (INTEGER 0/1, AUTHORED in 0023_checkin_test_mode.sql, doc 17 FR-22.3/ruling 40) marks a single check-in as a TEST check-in, taken while the invitation's `checkin_test_mode` (see `invitations` table note) is on; written by worker-user only, alongside `checked_in_at` which it already owns — the same check-in write path sets both columns together. `checkinSummary` and every future attendance export MUST filter out rows where this is 1 (OQ-34: never counted as real attendance); turning test mode off resets both `checked_in_at` back to NULL and this column back to 0 for every guest so marked (full erase, not just untagging) — entirely a worker-user-owned write, since worker-user already has both columns. worker-admin is NOT a writer or reader of `guests` in this change; see the `invitations.checkin_test_mode` note for the flagged, undecided question of whether an admin-triggered erase (add-on revoked while test check-ins are outstanding) needs a further widening here. Shared-write table (doc 03 §1): worker-user owns CRUD + check-in; worker-undangan must write nothing except opened_at/opened_count (the open-tracking increment in loadStore()/data.ts). worker-landing reads for demo-guest-token resolution in catalog.ts's loadStore() (one of the 3 reader corrections). `checked_in_by`/`checkin_method` are PLANNED (0014_checkin_attribution.sql); `updated_at` is PLANNED (doc 02 audit-field delta).

rsvp.note: worker-undangan writes guest submissions (upsert per guest_id); worker-user moderates/deletes. No column split called out in doc 03 §1 for this group.

wishes.note: worker-undangan writes guest submissions (token optional, guest_id nullable); worker-user moderates/deletes.

gifts.note: worker-undangan writes guest submissions (token optional); worker-user moderates/deletes.

templates.note: Global template catalog, admin-curated, unrestricted read by all 3 other services.

wa_templates.note: Global WA message presets, admin-curated. event_type->tag additive rename (BE-wl-04, 2026-09-21) shipped as `0026_event_label_rename.sql` (renumbered from the originally planned 0019 — see the `invitations` table note above for why) does not change ownership since worker-admin already has unrestricted '*' write covering the new `tag` column too; `event_type` is NOT dropped by this migration (that is BE-wl-06).

testimonials.note: AUTHORED in 0016_testimonials.sql (locked, not yet applied to the remote D1). Columns: id, name, event_label, quote, is_visible, sort_order, client_id/invitation_id (optional traceability, ON DELETE SET NULL), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Ownership unchanged: worker-admin is the sole writer (moderation CRUD), the other 3 apps may read.

invitation_domains.note: BE-mono-25 (approved by Pram): worker-landing gains an INSERT-ONLY grant so the provisioning batch (BE-wl-35) can create the `pending` row for a domain bought at checkout (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(domain) DO NOTHING); it writes nothing afterwards. ownership.json is column-scoped with no verb scoping (BE-mono-13), so the insert-only intent is enforced by worker-landing's repository types, not by the runtime guard; the column list is landing's creation set, and it deliberately EXCLUDES provider_ref, verification_details, verified_at, registered_at, expires_at, expiry_notified_at and removed_reason (staff/lifecycle columns). `order_id`, `price_idr`, `term_months` (and registered_at/expires_at/expiry_notified_at/removed_reason) are AUTHORED by BE-wl-34 (not yet in migrations.lock.json). worker-admin keeps '*', which already covers UPDATE of `domain` (staff changing the desired name, OQ-16) and the new registered_at/expires_at/removed_reason columns; worker-user unchanged ('*', request/insert for BE-user-15); worker-undangan stays READ-only (host resolution reads domain/status/expires_at). Original note: AUTHORED in 0017_custom_domains.sql (locked, not yet applied to the remote D1), with the `kind` (managed/byo) column folded in from the start. Columns: id, invitation_id (UNIQUE), domain (UNIQUE NOCASE), kind, status, provider_ref, verification_details, requested_at, verified_at, created_at, updated_at. worker-user requests a domain, worker-admin verifies/activates/removes it. JUDGMENT CALL: doc 12/03 describe this as a workflow-state distinction (who may move the domain through which status), not a column-level restriction, and neither doc gives this planned table's exact column list — kept as unrestricted '*' for both writers after authoring 0017 (the real column list contains no security-sensitive secret column, so no column split was introduced); revisit if a security-sensitive column (e.g. a verification secret) is added.

admins.note: No other service is a declared reader per doc 03 §1's matrix ('—'). worker-undangan's schema mirror must not define this table at all (R5).
